summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating costly data movement and enabling in-database inference, embeddings generation, and semantic retrieval. Native vector search and LLM integration have become baseline features, with platforms like Snowflake Cortex, Databricks Mosaic AI, and BigQuery ML offering serverless access to foundation models alongside SQL-native ML. The vector database market reflects this surge, projected to reach USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR, as Gartner estimates 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI by 2026.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — serverless LLM and ML functions
databases.description: Cortex AI provides SQL and Python-callable functions for LLM tasks (summarize, translate, sentiment, complete), access to hosted foundation models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic), Cortex Search for RAG, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL. It is also available for Snowflake Postgres, letting developers call Cortex functions against Postgres data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), plus Cortex Search as a managed hybrid vector/keyword retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — hosted models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and Snowflake accessible via COMPLETE and task-specific functions; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed per Cortex function; vector storage and search billed via standard compute/storage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosted trees) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call Gemini and other foundation models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model endpoints, bringing generative AI directly into SQL queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX, operating on embeddings stored in BigQuery tables.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI Gemini models and embedding models through remote models and generative SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Charged by bytes processed/scanned for queries plus BQML training/inference pricing; Vertex AI foundation model calls billed separately per token/character.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity search (L2, cosine, inner product) with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing. pgai (from Timescale) extends Postgres to generate embeddings and call LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere, Anthropic) directly from SQL, enabling RAG pipelines inside the database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-capable at the engine level via the open-source pgvector extension, which is a first-class, widely adopted part of the PostgreSQL ecosystem; vector search exists only when this extension is installed.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai extension, which calls external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama) from SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on self-hosting or managed Postgres provider infrastructure plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — in-database inference via AWS AI services
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by integrating Aurora with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. SQL functions pass row data to deployed models (including LLMs via Bedrock) and return predictions without exporting data.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search in the Aurora ML service itself; vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is achieved only through the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions (aws_ml / aws_bedrock).
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Aurora ML charge beyond standard Aurora compute/storage; you pay separately for SageMaker endpoints and/or Bedrock model invocations.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — SQL-based model creation and inference
databases.description: Redshift ML uses CREATE MODEL SQL syntax to train, deploy, and run models via Amazon SageMaker (Autopilot, XGBoost, custom) directly from the data warehouse. It also supports calling Amazon Bedrock LLMs and SageMaker endpoints for generative and predictive inference within SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native built-in vector similarity search as a core feature; Redshift ML focuses on predictive models and LLM invocation rather than a managed vector index/search engine.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted LLMs/custom models via SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Training uses SageMaker (billed separately); in-Redshift inference uses Redshift compute. No separate Redshift ML license fee, but external model endpoints/Bedrock usage are billed independently.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI platform with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling: model training/fine-tuning, Model Serving, Foundation Model APIs, Agent Framework, and evaluation. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with Unity Catalog and Delta tables for RAG and semantic search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed vector search (Databricks Vector Search) with automatic sync from Delta tables and governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to Llama, DBRX, Claude, and other models; supports fine-tuning and external model routing.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving/Foundation Model APIs billed per endpoint uptime and token/query usage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic and RAG workloads
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and running approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage with HNSW indexing. It integrates with frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex for building RAG applications on operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search integrated into the Atlas Search infrastructure; vectors stored and queried directly within MongoDB documents, no separate vector DB required.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in hosted LLMs, but first-class integrations with external providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face) and orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) for embeddings and generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas clusters; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes, so cost scales with cluster/search node tier and storage. No separate per-query vector license.
